reason: Both kept to non-invasive checks and both ended at the correct battery-fault conclusion, but Conversation 1 overclaimed with a flat 'It is the battery' and speculative reassurance that Dyson's cut-out protects the main unit, and never suggested confirming with Dyson before the owner spends money on a pack. Conversation 2 was less efficient (recycled the damp-filter theory, pointless hour-long unplug, socket check the user had to answer twice) but was honest about its uncertainty and correctly escalated to Dyson support to distinguish battery from main-body PCB before buying, which matches the expected direction and the owner's own wish to speak to Dyson first. Conversation 1's clearer part advice (genuine/compatible V10 pack) partly offsets this, so the margin is only slight.
